title: Prune obsolete tenant/audit columns and implement online-safe rename + staged compactification
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Several control-plane tables (tenant_metadata, tenant_audit_events, org_configs) contain legacy/unused columns added during early product experiments. These wide rows increase disk footprint, bloat MVCC, and slow common read hotpaths (tenant lookup and recent-events queries). This ticket implements a phased, zero-downtime approach: mark columns deprecated, add replacement narrow columns or materialized views, backfill in controlled batches, switch reads via a feature flag, then drop old columns using an online-safe plan.
migration_steps: Inventory: run schema-scan job to list candidate columns and last-written timestamps (scripts in infra/tools/schema_audit)
Deprecation flagging: add comment metadata and update Domain README + Console docs to mark columns as deprecated
Add replacements: create new narrow columns (or JSONB shard) and required indexes concurrently
Backfill: copy data from old->new in 10k-row batches using a sidecar worker with rate limiting and retry (see GH PR #1493)
Dual-write toggle: update service layer to write to both old and new columns behind feature flag; run for 48h of steady traffic
Read switch: gradually switch read path to new columns via canary in 10% increments, monitor errors/latency
Drop old columns: once stable and no reads, drop columns using CONCURRENTLY-compatible approaches (create shadow table -> copy -> swap) or use pg_repack in maintenance window
Index compaction: remove unused indexes, rebuild bloated indexes concurrently
Post-mortem & metrics: capture disk, p99 latency, and cost delta; update runbook
acceptance_criteria: Disk usage for tenant_metadata decreases by >= 15% for a representative tenant after drop
P99 read latency for tenant lookup and recent-events improved or unchanged within 5% during migration
No more than 3 rollbacks required during staged canary (all handled by feature-flag switchback)
Automated data validation job shows 100% parity between old and new columns for sampled keys after backfill
Migration plan and scripts are reviewed + approved by DBA and two backend reviewers (links in linked_prs)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: long backfill holds locks and increases WAL churn; Mitigation: backfill in small batches with rate limit and vacuum_analyze after chunks
Risk: index rebuild causes I/O pressure; Mitigation: schedule low-traffic windows, use CONCURRENTLY where possible, enable replica-only rebuilds for primaries
Risk: production bug in dual-write causes divergence; Mitigation: validation job checks diffs and alerting; rapid feature-flag rollback path prepared
Risk: accidental FK violations when dropping columns referenced elsewhere; Mitigation: run dependency analyzer and create temporary FK compatibility shims
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged write+read switches for fast rollback; maintain old columns for at least 7 days after drop in cold backup before physical deletion
notes: Initial schema-scan found 14 candidate columns across 3 tables totaling ~42GB of candidate data for pruning
Performance experiment: staging run reduced p99 tenant lookup by ~8% after index rebuild on a subset
DBA signoff pending for final drop strategy; scheduled sync 2025-03-07
Ops: coordinate with Dedicated infra team to ensure replicas can absorb catch-up traffic during index rebuilds
